summary: Backend-only testing of JWT auth, admin CRUD, push notifications, and notifications listing. 25/25 pytest tests PASS (100%) against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. All requested scenarios verified: (1) both seed admins can log in and receive JWT with role=admin, (2) wrong password → 401, (3) /auth/register creates role=user/plan=free and returns TokenOut, duplicate email → 400, (4) /auth/me works with valid token and correctly returns 401 for missing/invalid/bad-scheme, (5) /admin/users returns list for admin (403 for regular user), (6) POST/PATCH/DELETE admin users flows work end-to-end including password rotation (verified via re-login), plan/plan_status/is_active updates, and (7) self-guardrails all enforced (demote self → 400, disable self → 400, delete self → 400). /register-push persists to db.push_tokens and returns 201 status=queued when EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is placeholder (upstream 401), and is idempotent on (user_id, platform) upsert. /notifications/unviewed returns list with category/query joined from searches and no _id leaked. /notifications/mark-all-viewed returns updated_count and subsequent list is empty. /search/process end-to-end still works (created + cleaned up test search).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1213 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into modules: auth.py (JWT + password + get_current_user + require_admin), admin_users.py (admin CRUD), push.py (register-push + send_push), agents.py (SpecializedAgent + subclasses), search.py (search endpoints). Not blocking but improves maintainability.
Email normalization is applied on write (body.email.lower()) but the Pydantic UserOut returns whatever is stored. Consistent, but note that email comparison in tests must be case-insensitive.

_push_client is a module-level httpx.AsyncClient created at import time — good for connection pooling, but has no explicit close on app shutdown (only mongo client is closed). Non-critical but worth adding to the shutdown handler.

register-push swallows relay errors (returns 201 with status=queued) — this is intentional per the docstring and expected behavior in dev (EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder). MOCKED integration is clearly labeled and the local upsert works.
get_current_user reads Authorization header manually via Depends(Header). Consider switching to fastapi.security.HTTPBearer for consistent OpenAPI docs. Non-blocking.
seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral users with TEST_ prefix and lowercase emails; each is either deleted at the end of its class (test_admin_delete_other_user cleans up the admin-created user) or left as an idempotent registered user. The two seed admins are untouched (never demoted/deleted). Test search created via /search/process is deleted at end of TestSearchProcess.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth+admin+push endpoints all verified with 100% pass rate against public URL https://jarvis-assistant-603.preview.emergentagent.com/api. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_auth_admin_push.py for regression. EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is placeholder so register-push returns status=queued (this is expected and MOCKED). If the frontend flows need testing next, focus on: (1) login screen accepting both admin credentials, (2) /admin route rendering user list with role/plan badges, (3) /notifications screen listing unread search results and clearing them, (4) push token registration flow on first app open (POST /api/register-push).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Initial test failures were purely test-script issues (backend correctly lowercases emails on write, but assertions compared against the original mixed-case string). Fixed by lowercasing in the test data and using case-insensitive comparisons. Also moved pytest.<attr> assignments before assertions so dependent tests can proceed even if a downstream assertion in the same test fails.
